title: Relative Pronouns
description: Learn to use relative pronouns (que, quien, el cual, donde, cuyo) to connect ideas in Spanish.

grammar.title: Que — The Most Common Relative Pronoun
grammar.content:
QUE is the most versatile relative pronoun in Spanish:

1. For people and things:
El hombre que trabaja aqui. (The man who works here.)
El libro que lei. (The book that I read.)

2. After prepositions (people or things):
La persona con que hablaste. (The person with whom you spoke.)
La ciudad en que vivo. (The city in which I live.)

3. In superlative constructions:
El mejor libro que he ledo. (The best book that I have read.)

4. After 'todo':
Todo lo que se. (Everything that I know.)

Note: In everyday Spanish, 'que' is used even after prepositions in informal speech:
La persona con que hable → more formal: La persona con la cual hable

DONDE is often used instead of 'en que' or 'a que':
La ciudad donde naci. (The city where I was born.) = La ciudad en que naci.

NEVER use 'que' after 'de' for possession. Use 'cuyo' instead:
El padre de Maria → The father of Maria
The man whose son... → El hombre cuyo hijo...
examples: La casa que compre es grande. (The house that I bought is big.)
El estudiante con que hable es mi amigo. (The student with whom I spoke is my friend.)
Todo lo que quiero es tiempo. (Everything that I want is time.)
La ciudad donde creci fue Mexico. (The city where I grew up was Mexico.)

grammar.title: Quien/Quienes — For People Only
grammar.content:
QUIEN/QUIENES is used ONLY for people, especially:

1. After prepositions:
La persona con quien hable. (The person with whom I spoke.)
El profesor a quien恭恭敬敬. (The professor to whom I spoke.)

2. In non-restrictive clauses (with commas):
Mi padre, quien es medico, vive aqui. (My father, who is a doctor, lives here.)

3. In indirect questions:
No se quien es. (I don't know who it is.)

CONTRAST with 'que':

RESTRICTIVE (essential info, no comma):
El alumno que estudia mucho passed. (The student who studies a lot passed.) → identifies which student

NON-RESTRICTIVE (extra info, with comma):
Mi hermano, que estudia mucho, passed. (My brother, who studies a lot, passed.) → additional info about known person

QUIENES is the plural form:
Los estudiantes, quienes vienen de Mexico, son amables. (The students, who come from Mexico, are nice.)
examples: La mujer con quien baile es mi profesora. (The woman with whom I danced is my teacher.)
Mi madre, quien vive en Madrid, viene manana. (My mother, who lives in Madrid, is coming tomorrow.)
No se a quien preguntar. (I don't know who to ask.)
Los autores, quienes vinieron de Espana, firmaron libros. (The authors, who came from Spain, signed books.)

grammar.title: Cuyo — Possessive Relative Pronoun
grammar.content:
CUYO indicates possession and agrees with the thing possessed:

Cuyo (m sing) / Cuya (f sing) / Cuyos (m pl) / Cuyas (f pl)

Translation: whose / of which

El hombre cuya casa compre. (The man whose house I bought.)
→ casa is feminine, so 'cuya' agrees

La mujer cuyo hijo es doctor. (The woman whose son is a doctor.)
→ hijo is masculine, so 'cuyo' stays masculine

Las ninas cuyas tarefas revise. (The girls whose homework I checked.)
→ tarefas is feminine plural, so 'cuyas'

Word order: Cuyo comes BEFORE the noun it modifies:
El hombre de quien/cuyo libro → correct: El hombre cuyo libro...

EJEMPLOS:
El escritor cuya novela lei. (The writer whose novel I read.)
La familia en cuya casa nos quedamos. (The family in whose house we stayed.)
Los estudiantes cuyos proyectos presentamos. (The students whose projects we presented.)
examples: El hombre cuyo coche compraste es mi vecino. (The man whose car you bought is my neighbor.)
La chica cuya fotografia vi es famous. (The girl whose photograph I saw is famous.)
Los profesores cuyos metodos admiramos vinieron. (The professors whose methods we admire came.)
No recuerdo el nombre del autor cuyo libro perd. (I don't remember the name of the author whose book I lost.)

pronunciation.title: Relative Pronoun Pronunciation
pronunciation.content:
que = keh
quien = kyehn
quienes = KYEHN-ehs

el cual = ehl kwahl
la cual = lah kwahl
los cuales = lohs KWAH-lehs
las cuales = lahs KWAH-lehs

donde = DOHN-deh
cuyo = KOO-yoh
cuya = KOO-yah

que vs quien:
- 'que' is unstressed, short
- 'quien' has stress on the end

cuyo sounds like 'coo-yoh', not 'kwyo'

donde sounds like 'dohn-deh', not 'don-day'
examples:
el cual = ehl kwahl
la cual = lah kwahl

exercises.question: Which is correct for 'The man who works here'?
exercises.explanation: 'Que' is used for both people and things. 'El hombre que trabaja aqui' = The man who works here.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Todo lo ___ se es esto. (Everything that I know is this.)'
exercises.explanation: After 'todo lo que', use 'que'. 'Todo lo que se' = Everything that I know.

exercises.question: Which is correct for 'The city where I live'?
exercises.explanation: 'Donde' is used for locations. 'La ciudad donde vivo' = The city where I live.

exercises.question: Complete: 'La persona con ___ hable es mi amiga. (The person with whom I spoke is my friend.)'
exercises.explanation: After prepositions for people, use 'quien'. 'Con quien' = with whom.

exercises.question: Which is the possessive relative pronoun?
exercises.explanation: 'Cuyo' means 'whose' and indicates possession. It agrees with the noun it modifies.

exercises.question: Complete: 'El hombre ___ hijo estudio aqui. (The man whose son studied here.)'
exercises.explanation: Cuyo = whose (possessive). 'El hombre cuyo hijo' = The man whose son.

exercises.question: Which is correct: 'My father, who lives in Madrid'?
options: Mi padre que vive en Madrid
Mi padre, quien vive en Madrid
Mi padre cual vive en Madrid
Mi padre quien vive en Madrid
exercises.explanation: Non-restrictive clause (with comma) for a person: use 'quien'. 'Mi padre, quien vive en Madrid'.

exercises.question: Complete: 'La autora ___ novela gan6 el premio. (The author whose novel won the prize.)'
exercises.explanation: Cuya agrees with 'novela' (feminine). 'La autora cuya novela' = The author whose novel.

exercises.question: Which relative pronoun is used after prepositions for things?
exercises.explanation: 'El cual' (and its forms) is used after prepositions, especially in formal Spanish. 'Que' can also be used informally.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Los estudiantes ___ proyectos presentamos fueron表扬. (The students whose projects we presented were praised.)'
exercises.explanation: Cuyos agrees with 'proyectos' (masculine plural). 'Los estudiantes cuyos proyectos' = The students whose projects.
